title: LLQ entry site
view: A distended abdomen from directly above, patient supine, head at the top, the patient's left on the image right.
teachingPoint: On the line from the umbilicus to the left ASIS, the inferior epigastric vessels cross about 40% of the way out; enter beyond two-thirds, lateral to them.
claims: Supine abdomen from above, patient's left on the image right (house laterality).
Dashed purple: the line from the umbilicus (on the midline) to the left ASIS, ticked at 40% and two-thirds (record).
Red dashed: the inferior epigastric vessels running up and medially from the mid-inguinal point, crossing the line at 40% (record: about 40% of the way out).
Teal: a 1.6 cm entry zone three-quarters of the way out, lateral to the vessels (record: more than two-thirds).
Standard adult anatomy: the ASIS about 12.5 cm lateral and 7 cm caudal to the umbilicus.
Labels: Umbilicus, ASIS, Inferior epigastric vessels, 2/3, Entry site.
Markings placed on the umbilicus and left ASIS traced on the painting; the vessel path is drawn from the record's 40% figure, not traced (vessels are not visible).

geometry.why: left ASIS on the image right
the vessels are medial to the entry
the entry is clear of the vessels
the vessels cross the line at 40%
